The narrator is developed as a complex character with rich sensory perceptions, internal thoughts, and evolving reactions to his environment (such as intentionally reversing his sleep schedule to escape the claustrophobic atmosphere). Meanwhile, the minor characters—such as the shipping clerk in Calcutta, the arguing Dutch officers, and the English girls playing the piano—are appropriately kept as flat characters. They are not over-explained, as their brief, one-dimensional presence effectively serves to establish the oppressive, noisy setting and motivate the narrator's retreat into solitude and the nighttime hours.
